name: Misoprostol (GI use)
mechanism: Synthetic prostaglandin E1 analogue. Binds EP2/EP3/EP4 prostaglandin receptors on gastric parietal cells → ↓ cAMP → inhibits histamine/gastrin-stimulated acid secretion. Increases gastric mucus and bicarbonate secretion, enhances mucosal blood flow. Replaces protective prostaglandins depleted by NSAIDs. Also has uterotonic effects (used separately in obstetrics)
dosing: NSAID-associated ulcer prophylaxis: 200mcg PO BD-QDS (with food to minimize GI side effects). Usually 200mcg BD or TDS sufficient. Take with NSAIDs throughout treatment course. Healing of NSAID-induced ulcers: 200mcg QDS for 4-8 weeks. Reduce dose if intolerable diarrhoea (100mcg QDS). Avoid in women of childbearing potential unless essential with contraception
contraindications: Pregnancy (uterotonic - causes miscarriage, uterine rupture, teratogenic if pregnancy continues - limb defects, Möbius syndrome). Planning pregnancy. Women of childbearing potential unless essential with effective contraception and negative pregnancy test. Caution: cardiovascular disease (theoretical coronary/cerebrovascular vasospasm), inflammatory bowel disease (diarrhoea)
interactions: Magnesium-containing antacids ↑ diarrhoea (avoid, use aluminium/calcium antacids if needed). NSAIDs: misoprostol used specifically to counteract NSAID GI toxicity. No significant CYP interactions. Other uterotonics: additive (oxytocin, carboprost - relevant for obstetric use only)
monitoring: GI symptoms (dyspepsia, ulcer symptoms - should improve). Diarrhoea (common, dose-related - may need dose reduction). Signs of GI bleeding (melaena, haematemesis). Pregnancy test before initiation in women of childbearing potential. Effective contraception. Consider H. pylori status (eradication improves peptic ulcer outcomes independent of NSAIDs)
pregnancy: ABSOLUTELY CONTRAINDICATED - abortifacient (causes uterine contractions, miscarriage). Teratogenic if pregnancy continues (limb reduction defects, Möbius syndrome, cranial nerve palsies). Women of childbearing potential: negative pregnancy test before starting, effective contraception throughout. If pregnancy occurs, STOP IMMEDIATELY. Separate obstetric uses (abortion, labour induction, PPH) - different indication
sideEffects: Very common: diarrhoea (30-40%, dose-related - often resolves with continued use, take with food, reduce dose if severe), abdominal pain, cramping. Common: nausea, dyspepsia, flatulence. Women: vaginal bleeding, spotting, menstrual irregularities (uterine effects). Uncommon: rash. Rare: uterine rupture (if used inappropriately in pregnancy), hypotension (transient). Dizziness, headache
pharmacokinetics: Rapidly absorbed, extensive first-pass de-esterification to misoprostol acid (active metabolite). Bioavailability ~90% (acid metabolite). Peak 15-30 min. Food ↓ rate (not extent) of absorption and reduces GI side effects. Short half-life (~30 min), but effect duration longer (3-4h). Excreted renally (metabolites). Minimal renal dose adjustment needed
clinicalPearls: Brand: Cytotec. MAIN USE: prevention of NSAID-induced gastric/duodenal ulcers in high-risk patients requiring long-term NSAIDs. HIGH-RISK: age >60, history of peptic ulcer/bleeding, concurrent steroids/anticoagulants/SSRIs, high-dose NSAIDs, multiple NSAIDs. ALTERNATIVES (often preferred): PPIs (omeprazole, lansoprazole - more effective, better tolerated, once-daily). H2RAs less effective. INDICATIONS for misoprostol: if PPI contraindicated/not tolerated, cost considerations (cheaper than PPIs in some settings). DIARRHOEA: main limiting side effect (30-40%). Take with food, start low dose (200mcg BD), titrate up. Often improves with time. If intolerable, switch to PPI. PREGNANCY: CRITICAL - teratogenic and abortifacient. NEVER in pregnancy or women of childbearing potential without effective contraception and counselling. Misoprostol separately used in obstetrics (medical abortion, labour induction, PPH management) - different formulations, routes, doses. GI use ≠ obstetric use. NSAID ulcer prevention: reserve for high-risk patients continuing NSAIDs. First-line: stop NSAID if possible. If essential: add PPI (first choice) or misoprostol. COX-2 selective NSAIDs (celecoxib) have lower GI risk, but cardiovascular concerns. Combination products: Arthrotec (diclofenac + misoprostol) - ensures compliance but fixed ratio. H. pylori: eradicate if present (independent ulcer risk). HEALING vs PREVENTION: misoprostol effective for both, but PPIs preferred for healing (more effective, better tolerated). Duration: continue misoprostol as long as on NSAID. OBSTETRIC USES (separate indication): medical abortion (with mifepristone), labour induction (unfavourable cervix), PPH management. Higher doses, vaginal/sublingual routes. NOT covered by GI formulation/indication
indication: Prevention of NSAID-induced gastric and duodenal ulcers in high-risk patients requiring long-term NSAID therapy. Healing of NSAID-associated ulcers (alternative to PPI)
